question: Find literature evidence describing strategies for improving the performance of SnO2-based n-i-p perovskite solar cells. Give the strategy, mechanism, and supporting citation.
final_answer:
Evidence base and tool limitations first, because they bound what I can claim.

TOOL AVAILABILITY (important): the literature tools described in the question (search, read_paper, sql) are NOT executable in this session — calling them returns "Model tried to call unavailable tool 'search'. Available tools: glob, grep, invalid, read, todowrite." The only literature evidence available to me is the three search outputs already returned earlier in this session. I could not run read_paper to pull fuller passages, could not query the `devices` table, and could not retrieve any passage beyond the truncated snippets shown. Everything below is taken from those snippets; nothing is added from outside them.

STRATEGY 1 — Metal-ion doping of the electron transport layer (Sn4+ incorporated into the oxide lattice)
- Mechanism: Sn4+ is incorporated into the TiO2 lattice as an effective metal-ion dopant with no secondary phases formed (by XPS and XRD); versus pristine TiO2 the doped film shows lower trap-state density and higher conductivity, giving more efficient photogenerated electron extraction and transport. The ETL is deposited by a low-temperature solution method, so the whole stack stays low-temperature.
- Citation: 10.1016/j.electacta.2017.12.108 (Electrochimica Acta; keywords: Perovskite solar cells, Sn-doped TiO2, Electron transporting layers, Low-temperature solution method).
- Caveat: this is Sn-doped TiO2, not SnO2. The same reference list also cites the dopant family as an ETL strategy: Mg-doped TiO2 boosting planar PSC efficiency to exceed 19% (J. Mater. Chem. 4 (2016) 15383-15389) and Nb-doped TiO2 nanorods for improved charge transport (J. Mater. Chem. 2 (2014) 19616-19622).

STRATEGY 2 — Chloride-additive (FACl) antisolvent crystallization on a SnO2 ETL
- Mechanism: antisolvent deposition plus an FACl (chloride) additive controls the crystallization of the perovskite on the SnO2 ETL. The antisolvent reference film shows small grains forming a capping layer on top of a 300 nm thick perovskite layer, a morphology the authors expect to increase the interfacial recombination rate with SnO2 — i.e. the additive is used to control grain/cap-layer formation at the SnO2/perovskite interface.
- Citation: 10.1002/aenm.201803587 ("Controllable Perovskite Crystallization via Antisolvent Technique Using Chloride Additives for Highly Efficient Planar Perovskite Solar Cells"), Sec. 2 Results and Discussion (passage on SnO2-based planar films; 300 nm perovskite layer).

STRATEGY 3 — Perovskite surface passivation with adamantylammonium chloride (ADAHCl), layered onto strategy 2
- Mechanism: passivation of the perovskite surface with 1-adamantylamine hydrochloride further improves film quality by retarding surface recombination, evidenced by photoluminescence (PL) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS).
- Result and citation: a SnO2-based planar PSC with PCE 21.2%, low hysteresis, open-circuit voltage 1152 mV, and retention of 88% of its initial PCE after 700 h (test condition truncated in the retrieved snippet). Citation: 10.1002/aenm.201803587, Sec. 1 Introduction passage.

STRATEGY 4 — Interface engineering / degradation-suppression at the perovskite–ETL and perovskite–HTL contacts (diagnosis from retrieved text)
- Mechanism as described: (i) iodide oxidation to I2 near the interface between the perovskite and the top electron-transport layer; (ii) detachment of the perovskite from the bottom hole-transport layer, limiting photogenerated carrier collection at the contact; (iii) modification of the perovskite surface electronic structure that raises the hole-extraction barrier and causes energy loss. These are the failure modes any SnO2 n-i-p improvement strategy must suppress.
- Citation: 10.1016/j.nanoen.2018.10.011, Sec. 3 Discussion.
- Caveat: only the degradation-diagnosis passages were retrieved. The specific remedy, device architecture, and performance numbers of that paper could not be established without read_paper.

STRATEGY 5 (contextual, from retrieved reference lists rather than body text) — inorganic charge extraction layers and deliberate interface engineering as routes to efficient and stable PSCs; cited as reference [17] and [35] in 10.1016/j.electacta.2017.12.108: "Efficient and stable large-area perovskite solar cells with inorganic charge extraction layers", Science 350 (2015) 944-948 (Chen, Wu, Yue, Liu, Zhang, Yang, Chen, Bi, Ashraful, Grätzel); "Interface engineering of highly efficient perovskite solar cells", Science 345 (2014) 542-546 (Zhou et al.).

WHAT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED
- Li-doped SnO2 (or K/Rb-doped SnO2) as a conductivity-enhancement strategy: the dedicated query returned only Sn-doped TiO2 papers (10.1016/j.electacta.2017.12.108) and TiO2-dopant references. No Li-doped SnO2 evidence exists in the retrieved passages, and no Li/SnO2 conductivity, trap-density or PCE values can be quoted.
- Self-assembled-monolayer (e.g. phosphonic-acid) modification of the SnO2 surface itself: the query returned instead the perovskite-side ADAHCl/FACl passivation of 10.1002/aenm.201803587. No SAM-on-SnO2 evidence was retrieved.
- Quantitative SnO2-specific parameters (carrier density, electron affinity, band offset, trap density, dopant concentration) and any SnO2-only device records from the `devices` database: the sql tool was unavailable and no such values appear in the snippets.
- The single truncated hit 10.1038/ncomms15330 (Nat. Commun.; only the reference string "...lead iodide perovskite solar cells with silve..." was retrieved) could not be identified, so it is not cited as evidence for any strategy.
- The fifth hit in the first search was a duplicate of 10.1002/aenm.201803587 (truncated), and several snippets end mid-sentence (e.g. the 700 h retention test, and the expected recombination behavior of the small-grain capping layer on the 300 nm film); the missing text was not retrievable with the tools available.

STRATEGY 1 — Metal-ion doping of the electron transport layer (Sn4+ incorporated into the oxide lattice)
- Mechanism: Sn4+ is incorporated into the TiO2 lattice as an effective metal-ion dopant with no secondary phases formed (by XPS and XRD); versus pristine TiO2 the doped film shows lower trap-state density and higher conductivity, giving more efficient photogenerated electron extraction and transport. The ETL is deposited by a low-temperature solution method, so the whole stack stays low-temperature.
- Citation: 10.1016/j.electacta.2017.12.108 (Electrochimica Acta; keywords: Perovskite solar cells, Sn-doped TiO2, Electron transporting layers, Low-temperature solution method).
- Caveat: this is Sn-doped TiO2, not SnO2. The same reference list also cites the dopant family as an ETL strategy: Mg-doped TiO2 boosting planar PSC efficiency to exceed 19% (J. Mater. Chem. 4 (2016) 15383-15389) and Nb-doped TiO2 nanorods for improved charge transport (J. Mater. Chem. 2 (2014) 19616-19622).

STRATEGY 2 — Chloride-additive (FACl) antisolvent crystallization on a SnO2 ETL
- Mechanism: antisolvent deposition plus an FACl (chloride) additive controls the crystallization of the perovskite on the SnO2 ETL. The antisolvent reference film shows small grains forming a capping layer on top of a 300 nm thick perovskite layer, a morphology the authors expect to increase the interfacial recombination rate with SnO2 — i.e. the additive is used to control grain/cap-layer formation at the SnO2/perovskite interface.
- Citation: 10.1002/aenm.201803587 ("Controllable Perovskite Crystallization via Antisolvent Technique Using Chloride Additives for Highly Efficient Planar Perovskite Solar Cells"), Sec. 2 Results and Discussion (passage on SnO2-based planar films; 300 nm perovskite layer).

STRATEGY 3 — Perovskite surface passivation with adamantylammonium chloride (ADAHCl), layered onto strategy 2
- Mechanism: passivation of the perovskite surface with 1-adamantylamine hydrochloride further improves film quality by retarding surface recombination, evidenced by photoluminescence (PL) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS).
- Result and citation: a SnO2-based planar PSC with PCE 21.2%, low hysteresis, open-circuit voltage 1152 mV, and retention of 88% of its initial PCE after 700 h (test condition truncated in the retrieved snippet). Citation: 10.1002/aenm.201803587, Sec. 1 Introduction passage.

STRATEGY 4 — Interface engineering / degradation-suppression at the perovskite–ETL and perovskite–HTL contacts (diagnosis from retrieved text)
- Mechanism as described: (i) iodide oxidation to I2 near the interface between the perovskite and the top electron-transport layer; (ii) detachment of the perovskite from the bottom hole-transport layer, limiting photogenerated carrier collection at the contact; (iii) modification of the perovskite surface electronic structure that raises the hole-extraction barrier and causes energy loss. These are the failure modes any SnO2 n-i-p improvement strategy must suppress.
- Citation: 10.1016/j.nanoen.2018.10.011, Sec. 3 Discussion.
- Caveat: only the degradation-diagnosis passages were retrieved. The specific remedy, device architecture, and performance numbers of that paper could not be established without read_paper.
